item.text: I’m checking whether there’s still a refactor with real value left. At this point I’m targeting API cohesion and duplicated setup paths, not cosmetic changes.

I found one more refactor that’s actually useful: the code computes a `Codebook` internally but doesn’t expose it, so callers that need both orderings have to rebuild the tree twice through separate APIs. I’m promoting `Codebook` to an explicit API type and wiring the old methods through it.
The codebook is now a first-class API object, and the old convenience methods just delegate through it. I’m adding a focused test to prove callers can derive both orderings from one built codebook.
I’ve finished the API refactor. Next I’m recompiling and running both the demo and the test harness to verify the new `Codebook` surface didn’t change behavior.

Refactored [HuffmanCoding.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/033_huffman_coding/HuffmanCoding.java:8) to expose `Codebook` as a real API type instead of an internal detail. That means callers can build the Huffman tree once with `codebook(...)` and then ask for either `inTraversalOrder()` or `inSymbolOrder()` without recomputing anything. The existing `huffmanCodes(...)` helpers now just delegate through that API.

I updated [HuffmanCodingTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/033_huffman_coding/HuffmanCodingTest.java:4) with a test that exercises both orderings from a single codebook instance.
